references.text: Matthew describes the angel at the tomb with an appearance like lightning and clothes white as snow, parallel to the two men in radiant clothing in Matt 28:2-3.
Mark tells of a young man in a white robe sitting in the tomb, a parallel to the two men in radiant clothing in Luke's account (Mark 16:5).
John describes two angels in white sitting where Jesus' body had lain, corresponding to the two men who stood with the women in John 20:12.
At Jesus' ascension, two men in white clothes stood with the disciples – the same expression (ἄνδρες δύο) and the same type of heavenly appearance as at the tomb (Acts 1:10).
During the transfiguration on the mountain, two men appeared – Moses and Elijah – in glory with Jesus. The expression "two men" (ἄνδρες δύο) is the same as used at the tomb (Luke 9:30).
In Daniel's vision, a man appeared in shining linen clothes with a face like lightning, reminiscent of the two men in radiant clothing at Jesus' tomb (Dan 10:5-6).
Abraham saw three men standing before him – the Lord and two angels in human form, referred to as "men" (ἄνδρες), just as heavenly beings are also called "men" at the tomb (Gen 18:2).
Cornelius saw a man in shining clothes (ἐσθῆτι λαμπρᾷ) standing before him, an angel in radiant garment, similar to the two men in radiant clothing at the tomb (Acts 10:30).
The Lord's angel stood with the shepherds and the glory of the Lord shone around them – divine radiance connected with a heavenly messenger, as at the tomb in Luke 2:9.
